title: Royal Óbidos Draws Blood On Debut
title_candidates: Royal Óbidos Draws Blood On Debut
The Field Meets Its Match At Óbidos
theme: A brutal, beautiful debut for Seve Ballesteros's final design, which punished every player with at least one big number and reshuffled the Green Jacket race in the process.
tone: Wry and restrained, treating a viciously difficult new course like an act of aggression against six blameless amateurs.
opening_hook: Royal Óbidos, Seve Ballesteros's last design and TEG's first visit to the Lisbon Coast, greeted the field with water, wind and rather too many testing greens, and left not one of the six players unscathed.

round_story.subject: Gregg Williams survives two big numbers to post the best round of the day at Royal Óbidos
round_story.why_it_matters: It was, by the numbers, the best round anyone managed on the course's difficult debut — proof that survival, not smoothness, was the currency of the day.
round_story.shape: Gregg Williams arrived mid-pack in the Trophy race and immediately found trouble, a quadruple bogey at the 4th followed later by a quintuple bogey at the 14th. Between and around the carnage he strung together two hot stretches, gaining four shots on par over the 1st to 3rd and six more from the 7th to the 10th, with a recovery birdie at the 8th breaking a bad run. The net result was -4 for the round, the best net score anyone in the field could manage on the day.
headline_candidates: Williams Turns Carnage Into Best Round
Two Blow-Ups Still Produce Best Round
Gregg Williams Rides The Óbidos Rollercoaster
round_story.chosen_headline: Williams Turns Carnage Into Best Round
round_story.standfirst: A quintuple bogey at the 14th and a quadruple bogey at the 4th did nothing to stop Gregg Williams carding the best net score of the day at Royal Óbidos.

race_story.subject: David Mullin retakes the Green Jacket lead as Henry Meller's back nine unravels
race_story.why_it_matters: The Green Jacket race swung for the first time since round one, while the Trophy gap blew out to its widest margin yet — the two competitions moving in opposite directions off the same round.
race_story.shape: Henry Meller began the day three clear in the Green Jacket and eleven up in the Trophy, both leads looking secure. Drawing level for the Jacket at the 14th proved a false dawn: a triple, double, triple and double from the 15th sent him backwards, and David Mullin, level for the lead twice already that day, went through for good. The net effect of the round: Meller's Trophy cushion widened to 15 as his closest rivals fell even further away, but his Green Jacket lead is gone.
headline_candidates: Mullin Reclaims The Green Jacket Lead
Meller's Back Nine Costs Him The Jacket
Mullin Retakes Jacket As Meller Fades
race_story.chosen_headline: Mullin Retakes Jacket As Meller Fades
race_story.standfirst: Three lead changes in the Gross competition were settled when Henry Meller dropped ten shots across the closing four holes, handing David Mullin a three-shot cushion.

discovered_storylines.subject: Jon Baker's Trophy challenge collapses in three holes
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: He was the only realistic Trophy pursuer overnight; two holes at Royal Óbidos ended that pursuit and reshuffled the chasing pack behind Henry Meller.
discovered_storylines.shape: Jon Baker arrived at Royal Óbidos just 11 shots off Henry Meller's Trophy lead, the nearest thing to a rival. A quintuple bogey ten at the 2nd was followed immediately by a quadruple bogey seven at the 3rd, five shots gone to par in as many holes. Two clean pars at the 7th and 8th arrived too late to repair the damage, and he finished the day tied for third, his round the worst net score of anyone in the field.
headline_candidates: Two Holes Wreck Jon Baker's Charge
Jon Baker's Trophy Bid Falls Apart
Disaster Strikes Early For Jon Baker
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Two Holes Wreck Jon Baker's Charge
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Ten at the par-five 2nd and seven at the 3rd turned Jon Baker's overnight position as closest Trophy challenger into a share of third place, 17 shots off Henry Meller's lead.

race_state_note: Henry Meller's Trophy cushion widened to 15 net shots not through his own play but via Jon Baker and Stuart Neumann's collapses; Alex Baker's Wooden Spoon gap more than doubled to seven after a blow-up at the 6th and a bruising stretch from the 9th to the 12th.
